text:
tess: Heads-up — our Go sample app (onboarding flow) hit a weird stall in staging: workers stop advancing pages but no 5xx/429s. Throughput collapses. Repro attached.

ryan: any logs? quick synopsis of what the sample does?

tess: sample uses Go SDK adaptive-windowing + client-side backpressure + OIDC ephemeral token refresh every ~1s in our test. We also enabled aggressive prefetch (prefetch=3). Logs: ```
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z INFO token: fetched new token ttl=1.0s
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z INFO leases: renewing leases=5
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z DEBUG paginator: claimed cursor=cur-A
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z DEBUG fetch: started cur=cur-A slot=2
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z INFO token: refreshing token
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z DEBUG leases: release_and_requeue 2 leases due=auth_swap
2025-06-01T11:12:33Z DEBUG paginator: requeue cursor=cur-B
2025-06-01T11:12:34Z WARN backpressure: all workers stalled waiting for lease tokens
2025-06-01T11:12:35Z INFO bench: throughput drop 87%
```

tess: TL;DR: token churn + adaptive window resizing + prefetch = a coordination deadlock: token refresh causes immediate lease churn -> adaptive controller sees lower success -> shrinks window -> prefetched slots get cancelled and requeued -> but token rotation keeps releasing leases -> workers idle waiting for leases that keep flipping.

olga: interesting. so not classic duplicate-page loop — it's a liveness/backpressure deadlock. Did you see any retry storms?

tess: not really; requests rarely hit 429, they just get delayed and then cancelled. Customers see long tail latency and no progress.

ryan: reproducible locally? can we simulate token rotation without OIDC?

tess: yes I reproduced with a fake token provider that rotates every 800ms. Adaptive window shrinks to 1 and never recovers until process restart.

olga: quick ideas: 1) make token refresh cooperative: when token refresh in flight, pause adaptive shrinking and stall new claim attempts for a short jitter window (200-800ms). 2) clamp adaptive window shrink rate (don't go below 25% of previous in a single step). 3) reduce default prefetch from 3 -> 1 when lease auth churn detected.

docs-syd: for onboarding docs we should add a note about ephemeral tokens + adaptive windowing: recommend token TTL > 3s, or enable `REDWOOD_ADAPTIVE_AUTH_SAFE=true` to activate cooperative behavior.

infra-ops: we should also add observability: emit `sdk.token_refresh_inflight`, `adaptive.window_size`, `lease.release.reason` and an alert if `window_size < 2 && token_refresh_inflight > 0 for >5s` — that would catch the deadlock.

bench-bot: perf note: sim harness shows deadlock occurs when token_ttl < 1.5s AND prefetch >=2 AND adaptive_alpha > 0.3. Lowering alpha avoids aggressive reactions.

ryan: plan: short-term sample-app patch: turn prefetch default to 1 and add env `REDWOOD_PREFETCH_SAFE_ON_AUTH=true` to disable prefetch while token refresh detected. Medium-term: SDK changes: 1) cooperative auth stall with jitter, 2) minimum window clamp and rate-limit shrink, 3) expose telemetry metrics.

olga: unit + integration tests: simulate token churn and assert window recovers instead of shrinking to 1. Add a chaos test in CI.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=go/sdk-auth-stall, reviewers=@olga,@ryan. CI pending.

ryan: docs-syd, can you add a short onboarding blurb and sample config snippet? Something like: `# If your token provider issues very short-lived tokens, set TTL >= 3s or enable REDWOOD_ADAPTIVE_AUTH_SAFE`

docs-syd: on it. Will add a small example and note about prefetched slots.

infra-ops: adding metrics and alert. Will correlate with customer incidents.

olga: agree we should avoid changing defaults broadly. Make cooperative auth stall opt-in via env for now; flip in next major after telemetry.

ryan: thanks team. Tess, can you open the PRs and link them here? I'll review the SDK changes.

tess: will do. attaching short repro script to the PR. Thanks!
